title: The student “AI revolt” is mostly a myth. Business students just want to be taught how to use it.
excerpt: A three-year Kogod survey shows college AI use has gone from novelty to routine. Students aren't rejecting AI, they want to be taught to use it well.
content_html:
The boos at last spring’s graduations suggested a student revolt against AI. The data points the other way. Among business students at one Washington school, regular AI use has quietly become the norm, and the loudest demand is not to ban it but to teach it.

The figures come from a three-year survey at American University’s Kogod School of Business, shared first with Axios. The share of students using AI 11 or more times a week climbed from 6.2% in 2024 to 29% this year, the report found. More than 80% had used AI for coursework in the past six months.

Employers are pulling

Part of the pull comes from the job market. Interviews with AI questions rose from 11.6% in 2024 to 42.6% this year. Students have noticed. Prompt engineering is the top skill they want taught, and coding has leapt into second place, from under 4% to nearly 20% in a year. It reads like a shift from dabbling to the interview room.

The tools split by age. Undergraduates favour ChatGPT; graduate students lean towards Claude. Perplexity topped raw usage, though every student surveyed had free Perplexity Pro through a campus deal, which flatters the number. When students picked a tool, accuracy mattered most.

The anxiety underneath

None of this means students are uncritical. Nearly half of those at Kogod said they worried about academic integrity. In a separate Inside Higher Ed survey, 40% said they feared AI was eroding their ability to think for themselves. The message is not rejection. It is a request for clearer rules.

There is a paradox buried in the numbers. Brainstorming is the single most common use of AI, and has been for three years. Yet Wharton researchers found that people generated a wider range of ideas using their own thoughts and web searches than when they leaned on ChatGPT. The most popular use may be the one that quietly narrows thinking.

Schools are still working it out

Institutions are lurching between extremes. Faculty first tried to make assignments “AI-proof,” Kogod’s interim dean Casey Evans said, then gave up on it. The new approach is blunter: staff drop a student’s work into AI, tell them the result is a C, then coach them towards an A. She says resistance has been rare.

Elsewhere the mood is the opposite. Some universities have handed AI the job of watching students sit exams, and others, including Brown, have retreated to in-person, handwritten papers. Detection tools and cheating tools keep chasing each other. The classroom has not settled on an answer.

The Kogod numbers carry a caveat. They are self-reported, from 483 students at one school. But larger surveys point the same way: Inside Higher Ed found 85% had used AI for coursework, and Gallup put weekly use at 57%. The graduation boos were real. So is the adaptation. Students walking into an AI-shaped job market may not love it, but they are preparing for it.

content_html_zh:
去年春天毕业典礼上的嘘声表明学生对人工智能的反抗。 数据却指向相反的方向。 在华盛顿一所学校的商学院学生中，定期使用人工智能已悄然成为常态，最响亮的要求不是禁止它，而是教授它。

这些数据来自美利坚大学科戈德商学院为期三年的调查，并首先与 Axios 分享。 报告发现，每周使用人工智能 11 次或以上的学生比例从 2024 年的 6.2% 上升到今年的 29%。 超过 80% 的人在过去六个月中使用人工智能进行课程作业。

雇主正在拉动

部分拉力来自就业市场。 人工智能问题的面试比例从 2024 年的 11.6% 上升到今年的 42.6%。 学生们已经注意到了。 快速工程是他们最希望教授的首要技能，而编码已跃居第二位，一年内从不到 4% 上升到近 20%。 这听起来像是从涉足到面试室的转变。

这些工具按年龄划分。 本科生青睐ChatGPT；研究生倾向于克劳德。 尽管每个接受调查的学生都通过校园协议获得了免费的 Perplexity Pro，但 Perplexity 的原始使用率仍然居高不下，这让这个数字显得有些恭维。 当学生选择工具时，准确性最重要。

底下的焦虑

这些并不意味着学生不具备批判性。 Kogod 近一半的人表示他们担心学术诚信。 在高等教育内部的另一项调查中，40% 的人表示他们担心人工智能正在侵蚀他们独立思考的能力。 该消息并非拒绝。 这是对更明确规则的要求。

数字中隐藏着一个悖论。 头脑风暴是人工智能最常见的用途，并且已经存在了三年。 然而沃顿商学院的研究人员发现，与依靠 ChatGPT 相比，人们通过自己的想法和网络搜索产生了更广泛的想法。 最流行的用途可能是悄悄地缩小思维范围。

学校仍在研究中

机构在两个极端之间徘徊。 Kogod 的临时院长凯西·埃文斯 (Casey Evans) 表示，教师们首先试图让作业“不受人工智能影响”，但后来放弃了。 新方法更加直白：工作人员将学生的作业放入人工智能中，告诉他们结果是 C，然后指导他们获得 A。 她说抵抗很少见。

在其他地方，气氛则相反。 一些大学将监督学生参加考试的工作交给了人工智能，而包括布朗大学在内的其他大学则退回到面对面的手写试卷。 检测工具和作弊工具一直在互相追逐。 课堂上尚未得出答案。

Kogod 数据有一个警告。 它们是来自一所学校 483 名学生的自我报告。 但更大规模的调查也得出了同样的结论：《高等教育内部》发现 85% 的人在课程作业中使用过人工智能，而盖洛普 (Gallup) 的数据显示，每周使用人工智能的比例为 57%。 毕业嘘声是真实的。 适应也是如此。 走进人工智能塑造的就业市场的学生可能不喜欢它，但他们正在为此做好准备。
